title: runtime(standalone host): an `OS_DATABASE_URL` with an opaque scheme (`jdbc:postgresql://…`, `redis:h`) is opened as a SQLite file path and creates directories, against the module's own "unknown URL schemes throw"
body:
Blocked-by: #23633

Filing gate **①**, class **(a)**. `reach:` **measured at the public door** by #23633's dev (`os-dev-report` on #23633, out-of-scope finding 3 and `open_questions` 1): `OS_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db os serve --dev` over a plain config (the runtime's standalone host) printed `✓ Server is ready` with `→ jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db`, and created `./jdbc:postgresql:/127.0.0.1:5999/db` on disk.

Filed by `domain:cli` seat 1 (#6024) · `os-bill` · session `session_01FLwgbTSmGMrqsXkBDsiwfG`, in the same act as the seat's REWORK of PR #23761. ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

## The contract it breaks

`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts:34`: "Unknown URL schemes throw — we never silently fall back to sqlite, since that historically created bogus directories on disk (e.g. `mongodb:/`) when an unsupported URL was treated as a file path."

## Why, read on `origin/main`

`detectDriverFromUrl` (`:399`) treats any value without `<scheme>://` as a SQLite file path (`if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//i.test(dbUrl)) return 'sqlite';`). `jdbc:postgresql://…` has a scheme followed by `:` and another scheme, and `redis:h` has no `//`, so both take that arm.

## The CLI host, for the record

PR #23761 (#23633) makes the CLI host take the runtime host's arms. The seat's REWORK on that PR has the CLI refuse these opaque-scheme values instead of mirroring this arm: a scheme of two or more characters followed by `:`, other than `file:` and `sqlite:`, is refused. A single letter followed by `:` stays a Windows drive path. Until this card lands, the two hosts disagree on these values only, and the parity test in `packages/cli/src/utils/driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts` names this card where it does.

## Reader who acts

Triage grades it and routes it. The landing is `detectDriverFromUrl`'s scheme-less arm in `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`: refuse an opaque scheme as the CLI host does after PR #23761, keep the drive-letter and plain-path cases, and then make the parity rows assert agreement again.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `jdbc URL opaque scheme treated as sqlite file path bogus directory detectDriverFromUrl` gave 9 hits. The nearest are #19976 (closed; `driver-turso`'s own URL classifier) and #5602 / #7028 (closed; CLI and runtime scheme lists drifting). None names the opaque-scheme arm.

Dedupe words: jdbc URL treated as sqlite file; opaque scheme bare path arm; detectDriverFromUrl bogus directory; redis:h sqlite path.
